chunks: And from him, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the woman who circumambulates (tawaf) with the infant and runs (sa'i) with him, does that suffice for her and for the infant? He said, 'Yes.'
And it is not permissible for the man to circumambulate the House unless he is circumcised, and this has been permitted for the women. Narrated.

key_terms.السَّعْيُ: Running ritual between Safa and Marwah

ai.seo_question: Does a mother carrying her baby get credit for tawaf and sa'i for the child in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic flexibility (*rukhsah*) granted to women in ritual purity and physical requirements, contrasting the strict condition of circumcision for men with the permissibility of women performing *tawaf* and *sa'i* while carrying infants. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the physical burden of pilgrimage is alleviated for women, allowing them to fulfill the obligation for both themselves and their young children without the specific male prerequisite of circumcision.
